title: Reading short surahs: 108, 112, 113, 114, 103

bigIdea.text: Five short surahs, one at a time: Al-Kawthar, Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, An-Nas and Al-'Asr. Each has only a few short ayat, so you can read a whole surah in one sitting.

proper.text: Ayat: 108 has 3, 112 has 4, 113 has 5, 114 has 6 and 103 has 3. Suggested order: 108 → 112 → 113 → 114 → 103; 103 comes last because 103:3 is the longest ayah of the five (9 words).

provenance.source: Tanzil text, surahs 103, 108, 112, 113, 114 (ayah and word counts)

proper.text: In this text the basmala is printed before the first ayah of each of these surahs, without its own number (only in Al-Fatiha is it numbered as ayah 1).

provenance.source: Tanzil text: basmala prefixed to ayah 1 of surahs 2–114 except 9

proper.text: What to watch: the maddah in 108:1; the sukun endings in 112:3 and the merged ن in 112:4; the hidden ن before ش at the start of 113:2–5; the doubled ن with a hum at every ayah end of 114; the rounded zeros in 103:3.

provenance.source: rebuilt cpfair/quran-tajweed annotations (madd_munfasil, idghaam_no_ghunnah, ikhfa, ghunnah, silent) and Tanzil text for these surahs

proper.text: Echo each ayah after Sheikh al-Minshawi until you can read it without help, then read the whole surah alone.
At each ayah end: drop the final vowel or tanween (lesson 21), and give the long vowel before the last letter your chosen 2, 4 or 6 counts, the same every time.

memoryHook.text: One ayah, echo, repeat; then the whole surah alone.

extras.text: Short surahs are worth reading many times: each repetition trains your eyes on the same words until you read them at a glance.

note.text: The first word has a maddah and the next word starts with a hamza: hold 4–5 counts.
Every word ends on a sakin letter: close each one cleanly.
A bare ن merges into the doubled ل.
A bare ن before ش: hidden, with a light hum (Stage 2). The same pair opens 113:3, 113:4 and 113:5.
A doubled ن with a nasal hum of about 2 counts; every ayah of An-Nas ends on this sound.
One word: the و joins straight into the lam; the ٱ between them is silent.
Rounded zeros: the alifs after the plural waw are not read.

listen.note: Mapped by order (our lesson 30 → Nuraniah lesson 16) — please confirm. The video titles carry no topic, so check it fits this lesson and mark its segments when you watch.

questions.q: How many ayat does Al-Kawthar (108) have?
In this text, where does the basmala of surah 112 appear?
options: Before its first ayah, without its own number
As ayah 1 with its own number
At the end of the surah
explain: Only Al-Fatiha numbers the basmala as ayah 1.
It always comes at the start.
It is written before the surah.

questions.q: At the start of 113:2–5 a bare ن comes before ش. How is it read?
options: Hidden, with a light nasal hum, not a clear 'n'
explain: A bare ن is not a clear sukun.
An 'm' comes only before ب, with a small meem.

questions.q: In 112:4 a bare ن comes before a doubled ل. What happens?
options: The ن merges fully into the ل
explain: The shadda on ل shows the merge.
There is no pause sign there.
The ل is doubled, not silent.

questions.q: In 103:3 several alifs carry a rounded zero. What do you do?
explain: A rounded zero means never pronounced.
That is the upright oval zero.

questions.q: What is the best way to learn a new short surah?
options: Echo one ayah at a time, then read the whole surah alone
Read the whole surah at full speed first
explain: This stage is about reading the text.
Go in order, from the first ayah.

questions.q: Every ayah of An-Nas (114) ends with a doubled ن. What do you hear on it?
options: A nasal hum (ghunnah) of about 2 counts
explain: Qalqalah is for ق ط ب ج د with sukun.
The long 'aa' comes after the ن, not on it.

questions.q: How many ayat does Al-Ikhlas (112) have?
In 108:1 the first word ends with a maddah and the next word starts with a hamza. How long?
explain: The maddah asks for more than 2.
6 is for a maddah before a sukun or shadda.
One count is a short vowel.

questions.q: How do you begin 103:1, a single word that starts with وَ?
options: Join the و straight into the lam; the ٱ after it is silent
Say a hamza after the و
explain: The joining hamza drops after وَ.
The و belongs to the word; there is no pause.

questions.q: You stop at the end of 112:1, which ends in tanween damm. How do you finish?
options: Drop the '-un' and end on د with sukun
explain: The n of tanween drops when you stop.
There is no long vowel there.

questions.q: Reading these surahs alone, how long is the long vowel before the last letter at each ayah end?
options: Your chosen 2, 4 or 6 counts, the same every time
As long as your breath lasts
explain: It is a long vowel: at least 2.

questions.q: Why is 103 last in this lesson's suggested order?
options: Its third ayah is the longest single ayah of the five surahs
It uses letters you haven't learned
explain: Its basmala is printed like the others.
You have learned every letter in it.

provenance.source: Tanzil text: word counts per ayah, surahs 103, 108, 112, 113, 114

remnote: Basmala before surahs 108, 112, 113, 114, 103 in this text == Printed before ayah 1, without its own number
Learning a new short surah == Echo one ayah at a time, then read the whole surah alone
Bare ن before ش (113:2–5) == Hidden with a light hum (ikhfa)
Rounded zeros in 103:3 == Those alifs are not read
taskNow: Echo Al-Ikhlas (112) ayah by ayah after Sheikh al-Minshawi, then record yourself reading all four ayat, then press Play mine (step 5, Practise) and compare it with the reference.
